# Independent root audit: affine sampled support and zero incoming mass


`candidate b496d79ebd8db77a`.
This audits the scoped transport theorem and its exact example, not an
OC induction or any claim of critical-cap minimality.

1. The canonical hull preserves all actual integer fibers: it lies in C
and contains every original sampled fiber. Its projection is conv(P),
whose integer points already belong to P. Unsampled bulges of the
original C do not invalidate the canonical support plane; the note
explicitly avoids asserting that this plane supports the original C.

2. For the given direction u, affine support values put every sampled
u-face on one global supporting plane. Its restriction to a positive
full-dimensional polytope fiber has either a whole (d-1)-facet with
almost everywhere unique normal u, or zero boundary measure. The d=1
endpoint-counting case works separately. Thus physical restriction to
that global face equals the entire normal-u sector modulo null sets,
for eta and, by absolute continuity, for nu.

3. Normal preservation then proves BOTH no incoming and no outgoing
transport. Restricting source rows preserves their physical martingale
means and supplies exactly the full target sector. No inference from
only a supporting-plane mean, which alone allows incoming mass, occurs.

4. If P spans the base space, the canonical hull is full dimensional.
The common exposed face projects onto conv(P) and contains at least
one (d-1)-dimensional vertical face because its eta mass is positive.
The resulting n+d-1 independent directions prove it is a facet.
The lower-rank base case is correctly limited to the measure identity.

5. The straightening map keeps every integer coordinate and is an
isometry within each fiber. The mixed measure consequently has no
slope factor. The separate ambient factor sqrt(1+|a|^2), the intrinsic
Hausdorff dimension d-1, the q=0 reduced case when d=1, and zero-measure
smaller facet fibers are all correctly tracked. Formula (9) has the
correct plus sign for the note's convention h=a.z+b. Entire or empty
restricted halfspaces and positive boundary allocations remain explicit.

6. Affine support in every direction gives representation-independent
Minkowski interpolation at real bases of conv(P), by equality of all
support functions. This conclusion needs no arbitrary lattice-changing
coordinate transformation and does not assert an identity outside that
canonical base hull.

7. In the three-base cube example, the source masses are (.75,1.5,.75),
and the middle row (.25,1,.25) has mass1.5 and mean base1. Each target
base receives mass1, with the continuous point and mark unchanged. The
source is exactly the stated positive cap-indicator law. Its z^2 moment
is9/2 versus target5. After reducing a facet, it remains a nonconstant
interior volume law, whereas reduced own-fiber boundary measure gives
the fiber interiors zero mass. Thus vanishing incoming corrections do
not supply recursive boundary stress; the example is used only for
that assertion, not as a bad-depth certificate.

No corrections are required. The result removes the incoming correction
for an affine sampled support sector but leaves the bulk-budget and
recursive-optimality gaps open.

## Section4 append audit

The later classification of all nonvertical facets in the globally
affine-support, spanning-base case also PASSes. A nonvertical support
functional must attain the own-fiber support value at every point of
its exposed facet. If its remaining affine base coefficient is nonzero,
the facet lies in two independent hyperplanes, contradicting its full
facet dimension. Hence its plane is exactly the corresponding F_u,
which projects onto the full canonical base hull. Distinct such facets
have distinct continuous unit normals, so their own-fiber overlaps are
boundary-null, giving the claimed unique nonvertical ownership almost
everywhere. Projection-boundary vertical facets do not alter this
nonvertical ownership assertion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
